To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the community contextual predictors of endoscopy-based CRC screening in the USA are highly heterogeneous across states, and that this heterogeneity can be exploited to inform policy interventions to increase screening rates in the USA.

Medicare managed care penetration is associated with higher screening in some states but not in others, that prevalence of poor English language among elders in one’s neighborhood is associated with lower screening in some states and higher screening in others, and that prevalence of poverty among elders in one‘s neighborhood is associated with higher or lower screening in most states, but with lower screening in the vast majority.

(1) there is considerable variation across states in the community contextual correlates of endoscopic CRC screening; (2) interventions to address language barriers are needed most in some states and less in others; (3) Medicare managed care has not been effective in promoting endoscopy for CRC screening in the majority of states; (4) poverty has a negative association with CRC screening in most states, but a positive association in a few states.
